I ported `land --queue` and `xtask precommit` from VectorCraft onto the branch `land-queue-precommit-port`, tip 8aca3a79. `cargo xtask gate --branch` passed on every commit and the tip, `.githooks/test.sh` reports 0 failed, and nothing was landed, pushed or sent to codex-review.

One thing to know before landing: this worktree's hook path points at the shared checkout's `.githooks`, so my three commits went through the old pre-commit, not the new one. The new hook was run for real only inside `test.sh`, where it accepted a staged README change despite an unstaged compile error in bil-core.

## Commits
1. a7881dd0 `xtask: land --queue, ported from VectorCraft`. Ported from VectorCraft 9c455294, e9469b6f, b8959814, 33946ef0, 3da4b97d, 7bc10ca8, dbb7e2df, e400c269, 19a6ef7c, 73abe045, 440590c1, c86cc9a8, 32ef0528 and a7a4e002. The new code is in `xtask/src/land_queue.rs` and `xtask/src/land_queue/tests.rs`, plus small hunks in `main.rs`.
2. 1960fccf `xtask precommit and the pre-commit hook that runs it`.
   - **Command:** `xtask/src/precommit.rs`, `precommit/scan.rs` and `precommit/tests.rs`, ported from VectorCraft 09b2110f, 28ad543b, 5074bbb7 and 2eee2113.
   - **Hook:** `.githooks/pre-commit`, from d41ca2c6, 28ad543b, 9b0801c8, 41a3937a, fc10083a and 3b1c9e05.
   - **Parity:** `parity.rs` gains `parity_in`, so the check runs on the index rather than the working tree.
   - **Hook tests:** eight new cases in `.githooks/test.sh` plus one real-hook run.
3. 8aca3a79 `docs: land --queue and the pre-commit precommit check`. It updates `AGENTS.md` (step 7, the Gate section and the landing bullet), `docs/gate.md`, `docs/parallel-work.md` and `docs/sync.md`, and the prose went through avoid-ai-writing.

## Bug found in VectorCraft's code
`scan.rs` flagged its own table of temp-file suffixes as a fixed temp name, because the string `".tmp"` ends in `.tmp`. Running precommit on this port's staged files refused it at `scan.rs:238`, and a new test case failed the same way before the fix. A string that is only the suffix is now skipped.

## Failure cases covered
- **Each change fails on the old code:**
  - Before commit 1 the queue tests didn't compile. A mutation run (wrong phase for a failed check, skipping the killed-landing finish, dropping the partial file-update check) gave 5 failures.
  - On the old hook, all 8 new cases fail. On the new one, `test.sh` reports 0 failed.
- **Process killed mid-step:** a kill between moving the branch and updating its files is finished on the next run, from a move record and the pending-landing record. A worktree that took the branch mid-move gets the move undone. A failed rebase is aborted and the abort is checked.
- **Full disk or a failed file update:** a partial update keeps its record, so it can be finished later.
- **Zombies:** the `caffeinate` child is killed and reaped when the queue ends, and a test checks it is gone. tools/slot already reaps a dead holder.
- **Two callers racing:**
  - The branch is moved with `git update-ref` against its old value, so a branch someone else moved is refused.
  - A put-back never resets commits someone else added.
  - Two worktrees committing at once each keep their own tree in the shared precommit cache.
- **Signal mid-step:** if a precommit's `tools/slot` supervisor is killed with `kill -9`, the flock on `src.lock` keeps the next commit out until the first build ends.
- **Busy worktree:** a process working in the branch's worktree (`lsof`) refuses the move, and an `lsof` error counts as busy.
- **Missing tools:** the hook refuses the commit without cargo, rsync, perl or tools/slot. `commit -a`'s temporary index reaches the check.
- **Possible flake:** one early mutation run had 2 extra `--keep-going` failures. They didn't recur in 9 clean runs or a second mutation run, so I think it was machine load.

## Deliberately different from VectorCraft
- **Separate file:** the queue is in `land_queue.rs` and calls `gate.rs`'s `land` unchanged, because the other agent is editing `gate.rs`.
- **Phases inferred:** VectorCraft's `land_at` records how far a landing got. Ours infers it from the base, the landing record and `gate.rs`'s error text, and a failure it can't place stops a `--keep-going` queue.
- **Queue-only checks:** the stale-build check, the stop after finishing a landing that changed xtask, and `caffeinate` cover the queue only. A single `land` behaves as before.
- **Whole-file rustfmt:** precommit checks each staged Rust file whole, because our gate's `cargo fmt --all --check` refuses the whole file. VectorCraft checks only added lines.
- **Names:** `BIL_PRECOMMIT_CACHE`, `~/.cache/bewareilive/precommit` and the `bil-precommit` slot.
- **Last synced:** the commit stays at 01c95023, because the other shared paths up to 15cca858 aren't all checked. The paragraph now says these two pieces are taken.

## The `--host` seam
Passing `--host` to `land --queue` is refused with a message. When the build-host port lands, the hook point is `land_queue::queue_gate()` in `xtask/src/land_queue.rs`, and the refusal is in `land_queue::run`.

## Copy to other projects
VectorCraft needs the `scan.rs` fix (recorded as item 23 in `docs/sync.md`). It should go there first and come back, since VectorCraft holds the master. Nothing changed in tools/slot.

## Context7 lookups
- `/websites/doc_rust-lang_cargo`: the `executable` field of cargo's compiler-artifact JSON message.
- `/git/htmldocs`: `git update-ref` with an old value as compare-and-swap.
- `/websites/git-scm`: tried, nothing useful came back.

The gate speed work and the Studio build host are ported, on branch `gate-host-parallel-port` at tip `0737842e`. `cargo xtask gate --branch` passes on this Mac and with `--host studio`. Nothing was landed, pushed or sent to codex-review.

**Commits** (on origin/main `cbf8b449`):
- `999ec161` gate internals:
  - each gate builds in `<target>/gate` (`gate-tree` for the working tree) and holds an flock on `.bil-gate-lock` there;
  - `--locked` on every cargo step;
  - a `caffeinate -i` guard;
  - locked scratch worktrees with a watchdog, plus `gate --sweep`;
  - gate and land refuse an xtask built from other files (`srchash.rs`, `build.rs`);
  - stamp version 3, and `status` reads it.
- `18c9cd0a` stamp reuse: `land` reuses an earlier tip's stamp after a clean rebase (`gate_rows.rs`). `TestWorkspace` and `TestIgnored` count as builds.
- `149d8ade` the build host: `gate --branch --host H`, `land --host H` and `BIL_GATE_HOST`, with `xtask/src/gate_host.rs` and `tools/gate-host`. A host stamp is trusted only if its xtask was built from the tip and hashes the same as the tip's files.
- `0737842e` docs: `docs/gate.md`, `docs/sync.md`, `docs/parallel-work.md` and `AGENTS.md`, run through avoid-ai-writing in edit mode.

**What came from where:** VectorCraft's gate files at `902c5da9`, which include d363f3a3, 6ee79822, 9ab7d42f, 3ccf0f0e, 72b7743b, b2eaea67 and 9a4573a4. VectorCraft's main (`2f1a27ff`) has no later changes to these files. Not taken: `land --ci` (6be1af77), `tools/new-project` (8625a18a), `land --queue` and `xtask precommit`.

**Kept different here:**
- Every name: `BIL_`, `bil-gate-`, `refs/bil-gate/`, `bil-gate-host-*`.
- Our format step, a plain `cargo --locked fmt --all --check` run outside the slot.
- Our steps and path map, including `--ignored` at the tip, `verify --only`, parity and fuzz.
- `gate --branch --full` is still refused.
- I left out one VectorCraft test that checks its per-game mechanics files; we have one `docs/mechanics.md`.
- I did not copy VectorCraft's "never gate locally" rule.

**New here: a disk cap per Studio lane** (`tools/gate-host`). After each gate, still holding its lane, the runner measures the lane's target dir with `du` and removes it when it is over `gate-lane-gb` (a line in the caps file, default 4 GB). A dir it cannot remove fails the run, and no stamp is written. Two tests failed on VectorCraft's runner without the cap ("the lane over its cap was kept", "passed with its lane stuck over the cap") and pass now.

**Failure cases covered:**

| Case | How it is handled |
|---|---|
| A gate killed mid-step | Each cargo holds a copy of the lock, so it lasts until the last cargo exits; the watchdog removes the scratch worktree. |
| Zombies | A zombie counts as a dead gate, and the caffeinate child is reaped. |
| Pid reuse | The process start time is stored in the lock reason. |
| A failed remove or rename | The run, the run dir and the lane trim all fail; stamps are written to a temp file, then renamed. |
| Two gates at once | The target-dir flock, a `mkdir` claim for each scratch dir, and a lane flock plus a slot on the host. |
| Signals | The watchdog ignores INT, TERM and HUP; gate-host traps them. |
| A full disk | The lane cap, errors returned, and a host run with no exit code reported as "lost", which writes no stamp. |

**Gate timings:**

| Run | Range | Wall time |
|---|---|---|
| Old gate, this Mac, cold | 3 commits of main (6ca152f..cbf8b44) | 938.8 s |
| New gate, this Mac, cold | same range | 629.7 s (33% less) |
| New gate, this Mac | this branch, 4 commits | 1106.6 s |
| New gate, Studio, first build | this branch, 4 commits | 1165.2 s, using 1.6 s of this Mac's CPU |

On this branch, `verify` runs at every commit because every commit changes xtask, which is why it takes longer than the main range. I couldn't time the old main range on the Studio: that tip has no `tools/gate-host`, so a tip can be host-gated only once this branch is in it.

**Studio disk:** this project uses 1.8 GB in `~/Scratch/build/bewareilive/gate-host/lane0`, under the 4 GB cap, so it stayed for the next warm build. Its repository `~/GitHub/bewareilive/.git` is 25 MB. Each run's directory and state were removed. Free space fell from 58 GB to 48 GB during the session, but only about 1.8 GB of that was ours. The caps file there sets 2 lanes, so this project holds at most about 8 GB between runs. `docs/gate.md` says how to clean it up by hand.

**Context7 lookups:**
- `/openssh/openssh-portable`, ServerAliveInterval, ServerAliveCountMax and BatchMode: an unanswered keepalive makes ssh exit with 255. This confirmed the reattach-on-255 design; no change.
- `/websites/doc_rust-lang_stable_std`, `File::try_lock` and TryLockError: the lock is released only when every duplicated or inherited handle closes. This confirmed that passing the lock to each cargo as stdin keeps it held while a killed gate's cargo still runs; no change.
- `/websites/git-scm`, `worktree add --lock --reason` and removing a locked worktree: removal needs `--force` twice, which the port's sweep already uses; no change.

**To copy across:**

data.body:
The review of 3578ebf5 came back needs-attention with two medium findings (full text: ~/GitHub/bil-reviews/branch-3578ebf.md):

1. Enforce an absolute deadline for the attach handshake (xtask/src/gate_host.rs:1173-1176). Before the attach line arrives, every unrelated line restarts the full host.hello wait, and Wire::line restarts its timeout on every incoming chunk. An ssh startup that keeps printing diagnostics, or trickles bytes without finishing the handshake, never times out. Fix: track one absolute handshake deadline and pass only its remaining time to every read until a valid attach line arrives. Add regressions for repeated unrelated lines and for a partial line trickled byte by byte.
2. Bound the remote log reader's queue (gate_host.rs:992-1003). Wire uses an unbounded channel and allocates a buffer per read. A large failure log or reconnect backlog arriving faster than stdout drains grows without limit (AGENTS.md "Input sizes"). Fix: a bounded sync_channel for backpressure, keeping cancellation when the receiver is dropped. Add a test with a fast producer and a deliberately slow consumer that shows buffered data stays bounded.

Same rules: show each test fails on 3578ebf5. Make it one follow-up commit with no amending. Before writing it, check the rest of gate_host.rs for any other deadline that resets per line or per chunk, and any other unbounded channel or Vec fed by the remote, and fix those in the same commit. List them in your report. Main is still 4fc22aef, so no rebase is needed. Run `cargo xtask gate --branch` under tools/slot cargo 2 and report the tip. Don't queue the review, land or push.

**New commits (follow-ups, nothing amended):**

1. **55ff8ab9: bound the handshake, the output queue and the result** (review of 3578ebf5).
   - **Handshake deadline:** attach_once now has one absolute deadline for the whole handshake. Every read before the attach line waits only until then, and incoming bytes never extend a wait.
   - **Output queue:** the remote-output reader (`Wire`) uses `sync_channel` with room for 4 reads of 64 KiB. Dropping the receiver still stops the reader.
   - **Audit findings fixed here:**
     - Log-chunk reads reset their wait on every byte. Each piece now has its own fixed deadline.
     - The result after the done line was capped only by line count (about 20 GiB possible). It is now also capped at 2 MiB.
     - A host that sent its attach line and then dropped every connection reset the reattach window forever. The gate now gives up after 5 connections in a row with no new log. This replaces the old limit of 3 silent ones.
   - **Already bounded:** call and capture_within (one message each, stderr capped), the log carry buffer, and the absolute deadlines in call, capture_within and reap_within.
   - **Fail-first on 3578ebf5:**
     - chatty "the gate took 31.31s"
     - trickle "the gate took 31.25s"
     - "800 blocks of 64 KiB were read ahead with nobody reading them"
     - the 40 MiB result was accepted
     - greetdrop "still attaching again after 60 s"

2. **419197d7: a handshake ends at its deadline even with output queued** (review of 55ff8ab9).
   - **Fix:** `Wire::line` and `Wire::exact` now check their deadline first on every pass, so lines already queued no longer outlast it.
   - **Other loops checked:** capture_within, call, reap_within, start_remote's reattach deadline and the beat-thread join all check the clock on every pass already. follow_run's checks come after each attach_once, which this commit bounds.
   - **Fail-first on 55ff8ab9:** a fake host floods `yes` output into an attach whose `show` takes 5 ms a line. The old code gave "the attach was still taking lines 20 s after its 2 s handshake deadline". I ran it before and after rewriting the assertions.

3. **9663c41c: each scratch rebase claims a directory of its own.** This wasn't in your instructions, but it was failing the gate.
   - **Cause:** land --queue's scratch worktree name was `bil-land-rebase-<pid>-<subsec_nanos>`, and nothing claimed it. macOS's clock has microsecond resolution, so parallel tests in one process picked the same path.

data.body:
I fixed both failing tests. Looping the tests under load also turned up a real bug in `gate_host.rs`, which is fixed too. The branch is squashed into one commit, and `cargo xtask gate --branch --host studio` passed on the Studio.

**Branch** `hostflake`, **tip** `7747d418`, one commit on main `e1fcbe1a`. Nothing was landed, pushed or sent for review.

## Why each test failed

1. **`a_start_that_never_answers_gives_up_bounded`**: `preflight()` used `Host::call_limit` as its deadline. The test sets that to 0.2 s for `start`, so on a loaded host the preflight hit it first ("host dumbstart is not ready ... did not finish within 0.2 s"). The preflight now has its own `Host::ready_limit` (`READY_LIMIT`, 2 minutes, so real runs behave the same). The new test `the_preflight_has_a_deadline_of_its_own` fails on the old code with "did not finish within 0.001 s".
   - Looping turned up two more ways this test could fail. Under load, the fake ssh's count of how many times `start` was asked could come up short. And stopping the connection could kill the fake's `start` halfway, leaving a state where later starts said "started" with no run behind it ("never: the started run's gate").
   - The test now reads the number of asks from the error message. The fake runs `start` in its own process group, the way a real host's start outlives its ssh. The test waits for every start it began to finish, and a try where no start answered in time is run again with twice the deadline.
2. **`a_stalled_preflight_or_push_is_stopped_in_time`**: the 0.5 s deadline killed and reaped the fake's process group before it had stalled and written `stall-pid`, so reading that file panicked with NotFound. The group is already gone at that point, so the file can never appear, and waiting for it would not help. `stall-pid` now marks that the fake really stalled, and a try without it is repeated with twice the deadline, up to 8 s. Adding a 0.6 s delay to every fake connection (the new `ssh-delay` setting) makes the old test body fail at the same line every time, matching the Studio log.

## Failure cases covered

- **Pid files read half-written:** the fakes wrote `stall-pid` and `gate.pid` with a plain `echo >`. `kill -0` fails on an empty pid just as it does on a dead process, so a "was it stopped" check could pass while testing nothing. Both files are now written to a temp file and renamed, and `read_pid` rejects anything that is not a whole number.
- **The real bug, a zombie group leader:** stopping a process group whose leader had just exited reported failure. macOS refuses (EPERM) a signal sent to a group whose only member is a zombie, so `attach_once` gave up on a gate it should have reattached to. The new `stop_group` treats a group as stopped when the kill fails and `try_wait` shows the leader has ended. The new test `stopping_a_group_that_already_ended_succeeds` fails on the old code with "kill -KILL -<pid> failed (exit status: 1)".
- **`bytecut` sometimes failing with "the answer from bytecut did not end"** (1 in 50 loops before): the fake ssh exited before the run it started had closed the output. That is the likely cause, inferred rather than proven. The fake now waits for the output to close, as real ssh does.
- **Other tests:** no `land_queue` test has a sub-second deadline or reads a file a child process writes in the background. `a_host_call_is_bounded` does not depend on how fast the fake runs.

## Loop counts

All loops ran the `gate_host::` tests at nice 10, the priority the build host gives its gate, on this 18-core machine.

| Binary | Loops | Failed | Conditions | What failed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before (`e1fcbe1a`) | 50 | 13 | 24 CPU burners | 12 dumbstart, 1 bytecut |
| After | 50 | 1 | load 190 to 225, 48 burners for part of the run plus other agents | see below |
| After | 20 | 0 | load 130 to 150 | none |

The one failure after the fix was in `a_host_that_greets_then_drops_gives_up_in_time`: `settles()` ran past its 120 s limit while waiting for the host's own cleanup. This change does not touch that code, and the load was about four times what the Studio had. If it shows up on the Studio, that limit is the place to look.

## Gate

`cargo xtask gate --branch --host studio` passed on `7747d418` on the Studio, with a stamp written and no test failures. It had also passed on an earlier tip, `8250edff`, before the zombie fix and the fake-start changes were squashed in.

## Docs lookups

Context7 was out of quota, so I used doc.rust-lang.org's `std::process::Child` page. It confirms that `try_wait` reaps an exited child and keeps returning its status, and that `wait` keeps returning the same status after the first call. `stop_group` relies on that. The page does not state the `try_wait`-then-`wait` case directly; it follows from those two statements, and the new test checks it.

## VectorCraft

No copy is made yet: `docs/sync.md` item 29 records what VectorCraft should take.
- Its `a_start_that_never_answers_gives_up_bounded` and its `gate.pid` reads have the same races, and they need the fake and test changes.
- Its preflight has no deadline yet, so `ready_limit` should go across with item 26.
- It doesn't have the zombie bug, because it stops calls with `Child::kill` and ignores the result.

I didn't touch `tools/slot` or `.githooks/`, so no hook tests were needed.

One weakness is left unfixed in `tools/gate-host`. A start killed between writing its arguments and launching the run leaves a state that later starts report as "started" with nothing running. It fails safe: the attach reports `lost` after 30 s. The tests now avoid it rather than fix it.

The port was solid work, and every verified replay matching is a big step. The review of c841096e came back needs-attention with two high findings (full text: ~/GitHub/bil-reviews/branch-c841096.md):

1. [high] Resynchronise the cycle counter after the tally and respawn (loop_model.rs:330-334). State::step advances the frame during the tally, death and the respawn control delay without calling run_loop. On resuming, lp.t jumps to the current frame but lp.cycle stays hundreds of ticks behind, and the loop at line 377 then runs those skipped cycles on the current state. That pushes its clock into future frames and keeps moving or deferring newly fired shots, so every wave transition makes false scheduler debt. Fix: sync scheduler time and cycle state across those pauses, or advance the scheduler through them. Which one depends on what the original does: the probe logs' task countdowns across a tally or death show whether its loop keeps cycling, so check them, or take one probe run if they don't cover it. Add a regression that fires straight after a full tally and respawn.
2. [high] Check laser collisions at each executed step (loop_model.rs:410-418). run_loop can move a shot several times before State::step calls laser_hits once, so the hit positions in between are lost, and a shot at the edge is removed before any check. Example: a rightward shot at x 141 taking three catch-up steps visits 145 and 149, then is removed at 153; a Lander at screen x 149 is inside the hit boxes in between but survives. Options for keeping a full iCloud copy without iCloud syncing live git repos. My pick is A.
data.body:
Why it happens: iCloud syncs files while git and cargo are writing them (refs, index, target/). When two writes race, iCloud keeps both and names one '<name> 2'. Git then reads that as a real ref. The constant cargo churn is also why bird sits at 60% CPU.

A (recommended): work outside iCloud and back up a snapshot into it. Live checkouts go to a folder iCloud doesn't sync, e.g. ~/Developer/GitHub. A launchd job runs every hour (or when you ask) and rsyncs each repo, ignored files included, into ~/Documents/GitHub-backup. It skips only target/ and other rebuildable caches. It also writes a 'git bundle --all' per repo, so the history in the backup is one consistent file rather than a half-written .git. iCloud only ever sees a copy nobody is writing to, so no conflict copies, and bird calms down. Moving to a new Mac: copy the backup folder, clone from each bundle (or use the copied tree as is), done. Cost: the backup is up to an hour behind.

B: keep the repos where they are, but take .git out of iCloud. Rename .git to .git.nosync (iCloud skips names ending .nosync) and leave a one-line .git file saying 'gitdir: .git.nosync'. Point CARGO_TARGET_DIR outside iCloud too. Working files, ignored ones included, still sync live. History is backed up by an hourly git bundle into the repo folder. Smaller change, but worktrees and some tools assume a real .git directory, so it is more fragile. And conflict copies can still appear in working files, just not in git.

C: add a real backup tool next to iCloud (Time Machine, Arq or Backblaze) and move the repos out of iCloud. They copy open files more safely, but it's another product and more setup.

D: keep things as they are and add a check that finds and quarantines '* 2' files in .git every few minutes. That treats the symptom, and it can't protect objects.

If you choose A, I'd do it at a quiet point (no agents or gates running) with VC and AMB, since all three live in the same folder: dry run, a second check, a full copy kept before the move, move, then update paths (memory, crons, hooks, the Studio's gate-host paths) and verify a gate. About an hour. I won't start until you say which option.
